title: Operators in JavaScript
idea: An operator combines values, its operands, into one new value. Operators and operands together make an expression.

analogy.text: A calculator. The keys `+` and `*` are operators, the numbers you enter are operands, and every press yields one new value.
analogy.breaks: JavaScript operators also accept strings and silently convert types.

points: Precedence is the order operators run: `*` before `+`. Parentheses override it.
`+` joins text if either side is a string; `-` and `*` use numbers.
`==` converts types before comparing; `===` never does, so prefer it.
`&&`, `||` and `??` return one operand and may skip the right side.

parts.label: 1st: multiply
parts.note: `*` binds tighter than `+`, so it runs first. Arithmetic gives a number.

parts.label: 2nd: add
parts.note: Then `+` adds `fee`. Both sides are numbers, so this is addition, not text joining.

parts.label: 3rd: compare
parts.note: A comparison yields `true` or `false`. It binds tighter than `&&`.

parts.label: 4th: logical AND
parts.note: Runs last. A falsy left side (`false`, `0`, `0n`, `''`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`) is the result; otherwise the right side.

code.title: Operators that surprise
code.caption: Run it. Then change `port` to `null` and predict both results.

pitfalls: Input from files, forms or URLs is text: convert with `Number()` before adding.
`||` also replaces `0` and `''` with the default; `??` replaces only `null` and `undefined`.
Mixing `??` with `||` or `&&` needs parentheses, or it is a SyntaxError.

quiz.why: `+` joins when one side is a string, giving '34'. `*` converts '3' to a number. `==` converts too, so it is true.

takeaway: Operators follow precedence and may convert types: use `===` and `??`.

starters: What is the difference between == and ===?
When should I use ?? instead of ||?
What do truthy and falsy mean?
